description: The Giza Plateau is Egypt’s most-visited site and home to the three Great Pyramids: Khufu (originally 147 metres, built around 2560 BC), Khafre, and Menkaure (65 metres). The Great Sphinx, 73 metres long and 20 metres tall, is carved from a single limestone outcrop and faces due east. The plateau was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979. A private tour typically combines the pyramids, Sphinx, Valley Temple, and the new Grand Egyptian Museum located 2 kilometres away.
best_time_to_visit: October to April for cooler weather; early morning or evening for better light and fewer crowds.
practical_tips: Admission is about EGP 240 (approx. US$7) with an extra fee to enter the Great Pyramid of Khufu. Haggle hard for camel rides—start at EGP 200 but aim for EGP 50. Avoid photographing military or police personnel.

description: Luxor is home to the 134 giant columns of Karnak Temple, described as breathtaking, and the Valley of the Kings where you can explore pharaonic tombs. A hot air balloon ride at dawn offers a panoramic view for approximately US$40 per person. The temple corridor between Luxor and Aswan is best experienced via a Nile cruise.
best_time_to_visit: October to April; hot air balloon rides operate at dawn year-round.
practical_tips: Cover your shoulders and knees when visiting temples. Temperatures exceed 40°C in August—bring high-SPF sunscreen and cooling sleeves.

description: The rock-cut statues at Abu Simbel Temple in Aswan are visually stunning. Abu Simbel is typically included in Nile cruise itineraries as a shore excursion. The site is one of Egypt’s most iconic ancient monuments.
best_time_to_visit: October to April; the Abu Simbel Sun Festival is a popular annual event.
practical_tips: Abu Simbel is usually reached via a short flight or a long drive from Aswan. It is best combined with a Nile cruise itinerary.

description: The Grand Egyptian Museum is home to the golden mask of Tutankhamun and is located 2 kilometres from the Giza Pyramids. It is a must-visit for anyone interested in ancient Egyptian civilization and is typically included in Giza Plateau tours.
best_time_to_visit: Year-round; October to April is the most comfortable season.
practical_tips: The museum is a modern facility with extensive collections. Allocate at least half a day to explore it properly.

description: The Nile has been Egypt’s lifeline for over 6,000 years and remains the best way to experience the temple corridor between Luxor and Aswan. Standard cruises run 4 days and 3 nights with shore visits to Karnak, Luxor Temple, the Valley of the Kings, Edfu, Kom Ombo, and Philae. Extended 7-night cruises and traditional dahabiya sailings (8–16 passengers on twin-mast wooden vessels) offer deeper exploration.
best_time_to_visit: October to April; shoulder months of October, November, March, and April avoid crowds and scorching weather.
practical_tips: A Nile cruise gives immersive access to the Nile Valley. Book in advance during peak season. Dahabiya sailings offer a more intimate experience.

description: A century-old open-air market that feels like stepping into 'One Thousand and One Nights.' Open 10:00 AM–11:00 PM with free admission. It is most beautiful when the lights come on in the evening. It is a classic place to enjoy Arabic black tea and shisha.
best_time_to_visit: Year-round; evening visits are most atmospheric.
practical_tips: Cut souvenir prices in half. Be cautious of 'free guide' scams. The market is a great place to buy dates as local specialty souvenirs.

description: Egypt offers Coptic monasteries and Alexandria’s Greco-Roman heritage, which can be combined with other ancient sites into a single 10 to 14-day journey. Alexandria’s heritage adds a Mediterranean dimension to Egypt’s cultural offerings.
practical_tips: These sites are often included in extended itineraries. A 15-day trip gives enough time for Cairo, Luxor, Aswan, a Nile Cruise, shopping, and all major attractions.

description: Hurghada on the Red Sea is a diving paradise with 20m+ visibility. A snorkeling day trip is about EGP 300. Egypt’s Red Sea resorts have a unique and vibrant scuba diving culture with warm waters. Extended packages of up to 13 days include diving and coastal leisure in Hurghada and Sharm el-Sheikh.
best_time_to_visit: Summer for beaches and museums; winter for diving is also popular.
practical_tips: Avoid the Sinai Peninsula except for Sharm El Sheikh. Be cautious when choosing high-risk activities. The Red Sea is cool between December and March.

description: Crossing the Western Desert to the White Desert and Siwa Oasis is a unique experience offered in extended itineraries. The desert landscape provides a contrast to the Nile Valley and Red Sea coast.
best_time_to_visit: October to April for cooler temperatures.
practical_tips: Desert excursions require proper planning. A European-style round-pin adapter is a must. Pack stomach medicine as local food can cause discomfort.

description: As of August 2026, Egypt has fully implemented a digital visa-on-arrival system. You can use self-service kiosks at Cairo Airport to scan and process it, saying goodbye to waiting in line for sticker visas. The visa fee is US$25, cash only. You can also apply in advance via the official app.
practical_tips: Buy a local SIM card in advance or download Google offline maps. A European-style round-pin adapter is essential.

description: Stuffed pigeon is roasted with spices inside and is an Egyptian specialty. Grilled fish is a filling meal for about US$7. Koshary is the national budget fast food made of rice, macaroni, lentils, and fried onions. Dates are a local specialty souvenir. Arabic black tea and shisha are classic experiences at Khan el-Khalili.
practical_tips: Food is very affordable. Be cautious with local food as it can easily cause discomfort—pack stomach medicine.

description: In Cairo, you can stay in a room with a pyramid view for about US$28, with plenty of 5-star hotel options. Luxor offers high value-for-money guesthouses along the Nile. Hurghada is the top choice for relaxing at a Red Sea resort.
practical_tips: Hurghada
column9: October to April for peak season; book in advance.
column10: Accommodation is generally great value. Pyramid-view rooms in Cairo are a unique experience.

description: Camel rides at tourist sites might start at EGP 200, but haggle hard down to EGP 50. Cut souvenir prices in half. Don’t fall for 'free guide' scams. Avoid the Sinai Peninsula except for Sharm El Sheikh. Do not photograph military or police personnel.
practical_tips: Be constantly on guard against scams. Egypt is described as 'exhausting' due to the need to be vigilant, but the ancient wonders are breathtakingly stunning.

item_name: Gorilla Trekking in Volcanoes National Park
description: Rwanda is best known for gorilla trekking in Volcanoes National Park, where you can spend an unforgettable hour with mountain gorillas. The trek itself is exhilarating as you climb through dense forest in the first morning light. You are always accompanied by an expert team of trackers and guides. Gorilla trekking is one of the most moving wildlife experiences on the planet.
best_time_to_visit: Dry seasons: June to September (long dry) and December to February (short dry). Avoid March–May and September–November rains.
practical_tips: Gorilla-trekking permits are limited and in high demand during dry months—book well in advance. There is a 30% discount on permits in the offseason (November to May). Permits cost US$1,500.

description: Kwita Izina is the annual gorilla-naming ceremony, one of the biggest events of the year when crowds gather for the naming of newborn gorillas accompanied by festivities and celebrity visits. Aim for September to coincide your visit with this event.
practical_tips: This is a unique cultural and conservation event. Book accommodation and permits well in advance.

description: Nyungwe Forest teems with chimpanzees, colobus monkeys, and hidden waterfalls. The first rainy season from March to May is a good time to see chimpanzees, who come down from the treetops to feed on the fruits at this time of the year. Birding in Nyungwe Forest is superb year-round.
best_time_to_visit: March to May for chimpanzees; year-round for birding and canopy walks.
practical_tips: Nyungwe National Park saw a 20% surge in visitors, followed by Volcanoes National Park (+11.3%) and Akagera National Park (+6.8%). The park offers primate tracking, canopy walkway experience, and birdwatching.

item_name: Akagera National Park Big Five Safari
description: Akagera National Park is a conservation success story, now home to the Big Five (lion, leopard, elephant, rhino, buffalo), as well as giraffe, zebra, hippo, and crocodile. Wildlife viewing in Akagera is best during the dry seasons. The park stretches across a landscape of open grassland in eastern Rwanda.
best_time_to_visit: Dry seasons: June to September and December to February.
practical_tips: Akagera combines well with Nyungwe and Volcanoes National Park to offer a great safari. Spot hippos, elephants, and giraffes in Akagera National Park.

description: The Virunga Mountains offer hiking trails with stunning volcanic scenery. A one-week trip would allow you to take in Kigali’s sights and cosmopolitan food-and-drink scene, gorilla trekking, volcano hikes, and a trip to see the chimpanzees.
best_time_to_visit: June to September and December to February for easier trekking conditions.
practical_tips: Hiking in the Virunga Mountains is a bucket-list experience. Pack for a shower in any month as this is a rainforest.

description: Lake Kivu offers peaceful shores and islands, an unspoiled watery paradise for relaxation after wildlife adventures. It is located in western Rwanda and provides a contrast to the jungle and savannah experiences.
best_time_to_visit: Year-round; dry seasons offer better weather.
practical_tips: Lake Kivu is a great place to relax after gorilla trekking. It is often included in extended Rwanda itineraries.

description: Kigali is the gateway city to three of the country’s wildlife-rich national parks—Volcanoes, Akagera, and Nyungwe Forest. It has a cosmopolitan food-and-drink scene and serves as the starting point for most Rwandan adventures.
practical_tips: Kigali is widely regarded as one of Africa’s safest, cleanest, and greenest cities. It offers progressive environmental and sustainability policies alongside gender equality rights.

description: No discussion of Rwanda can take place without mentioning the atrocities of the 1994 genocide when an estimated 800,000 victims tragically lost their lives. Thirty years on, the healing continues in a country lauded for its resilience and reconciliation. This has paved the way for a new chapter in the nation’s history.
practical_tips: Visiting the Genocide Memorial is a powerful and important experience. It provides context for understanding Rwanda’s remarkable transformation.

description: Rwanda is a year-round destination for gorilla trekking, but just how muddy you’re prepared to get is another matter. The jungle trails are always a bit of a slip and slide, but come the rainy season (March to May and September to November) things are taken to a whole new level. Avoid the mud by visiting during the dry season (June to September), but with that comes bigger crowds. For a cheaper visit, aim for the offseason (November to May) when there is a 30% discount on gorilla permits.
best_time_to_visit: Dry seasons (June–September and December–February) for easier trekking; rainy season for dramatic photography and cheaper permits.
practical_tips: The months of June through February are the best times to visit Rwanda to experience maximum wildlife viewing and great weather. March–May are less popular months because of heavy rains, resulting in more challenging hikes and treks.

description: Rwanda is widely regarded as one of Africa’s safest countries for travelers and one of its most prosperous, cleanest, and greenest with progressive environmental and sustainability policies in place alongside gender equality rights. The country has come a long way from the not-so-distant genocide past and offers a very high-end safari-and-primates circuit.
practical_tips: Rwanda is astonishingly beautiful and sophisticated, almost unexpectedly so. It makes for a perfect addition to a more traditional safari experience.

description: Rwanda offers luxurious Big Five safari and gorilla experiences. A 7-night Rwanda’s Luxurious Big Five Safari and Gorillas trip ranges from C$22,135 to C$31,344 per person. Rwanda’s Ultimate Luxury 7-night trip ranges from C$38,958 to C$51,186 per person. The country offers a very high-end safari-and-primates circuit.
best_time_to_visit: Dry seasons for best wildlife viewing.
practical_tips: Book luxury lodges well in advance, especially during peak dry seasons. Rwanda’s safari circuit is known for its exclusivity and high-end service.

description: Table Mountain in Cape Town is described as spectacular. Take the cable car for panoramic city views. It is a famous landmark that people shouldn’t miss and is considered obvious but essential.
best_time_to_visit: Year-round; Nov–Feb (summer) is peak season for beaches and the Garden Route.
practical_tips: Table Mountain is a must-visit. Paragliding from Signal Hill over Cape Town’s cityscape and ocean is a unique experience.

description: The Cape of Good Hope is the southwestern tip of Africa with breathtaking coastlines. It is one of the stunning natural landscapes that South Africa boasts.
practical_tips: Combine with a visit to Boulders Beach to get up close with African penguins.

description: Boulders Beach offers the opportunity to get up close with African penguins. It is a unique wildlife experience near Cape Town.
practical_tips: This is a great family-friendly activity. Combine with Cape of Good Hope and Table Mountain for a full Cape Peninsula day trip.

description: Kruger National Park is the best place to spot the Big Five (lion, leopard, buffalo, elephant, rhino). It is a must-visit for wildlife enthusiasts. The peak season for safaris is between June and October. An ideal itinerary includes three nights in a private game reserve in Kruger National Park.
best_time_to_visit: Peak safari season: June to October.
practical_tips: Spend at least three nights at one of the lodges in Kruger National Park. A good amount of your budget should go to a lodge stay as it can really change your experience. Malaria risk in Kruger—take prophylaxis.

description: Addo Elephant Park is famous for elephant herds and is ideal for self-drive safaris. It is located in the Eastern Cape and offers a different safari experience from Kruger.
best_time_to_visit: Year-round; best for wildlife viewing in shoulder seasons (March–May, September–October).
practical_tips: Addo is great for self-drive safaris. It is famous for its elephant herds and is a more affordable safari option than private reserves.

description: The Garden Route includes Mossel Bay (a historic coastal town), Knysna (oyster paradise and forest hikes), and Tsitsikamma National Park (Storm River Bridge and ocean hikes). It is a classic road trip route along the southern coast of South Africa.
best_time_to_visit: Year-round; Nov–Feb for summer beach weather.
practical_tips: Self-drive the Garden Route. A 7-day highlights itinerary includes Cape Town + Garden Route + Kruger. A 5-day short trip covers Cape Town + Garden Route.

description: The Apartheid Museum offers a powerful and educational look into the horrors of apartheid. Interactive exhibits, personal testimonies, and archival footage provide a powerful experience. It is a must-see for anyone interested in South Africa’s history.
practical_tips: Allow 2–3 hours for the museum. Combine with a Soweto tour for a full day of historical and cultural immersion.

description: Soweto is home to Nelson Mandela’s former home on Vilakazi Street, the Hector Pieterson Memorial and Museum (commemorating the 1976 student protests), and the Orlando Twin Towers. A Soweto tour offers township culture and first-hand accounts of life during apartheid.
practical_tips: Visit the Hector Pieterson Memorial and Museum. Nelson Mandela House is a highlight. Soweto tours often include the Apartheid Museum.

description: The Hector Pieterson Memorial honours the young victims of the June 16 Uprising and remains one of Soweto’s most visited heritage sites. The museum documents the events of 1976 through photographs, testimonies, and historical exhibits.
practical_tips: Year-round.
column9: This is a powerful and important historical site. It is often included in Soweto township tours.

description: Shark cage diving in Gansbaai offers face-to-face encounters with great whites. It is a unique and thrilling experience available in South Africa.
practical_tips: Year-round; best visibility in winter months.
column9: This is an adrenaline-filled activity. Book with reputable operators who prioritize safety and conservation.

description: Hermanus in the Western Cape is a hub for whale watching. The southern right whale migration occurs from June to November. It is a hidden gem that more people should know about.
practical_tips: June to November for whale watching.
column9: Hermanus is considered a hidden gem. It is a great addition to a Garden Route itinerary.

description: Wine estate cycling in Stellenbosch offers a unique way to savor South Africa’s finest wines. Wine estates in Stellenbosch and Franschhoek are top attractions.
best_time_to_visit: Year-round; harvest season (February–April) is particularly scenic.
practical_tips: The Victoria & Albert Waterfront in Cape Town has many amazing restaurants right on the water. Wine tasting is a must-do in the Cape Winelands.

description: Paragliding from Signal Hill over Cape Town’s cityscape and ocean is a unique experience. It offers a thrilling way to see the city from above.
practical_tips: Signal Hill is a popular launch site. Paragliding offers stunning views of Table Mountain and the Atlantic Seaboard.

description: Overlanding focuses on adventure, exploring remote landscapes, and seeing wildlife. It is a unique way to explore South Africa, according to a destination specialist.
best_time_to_visit: Year-round; best in dry seasons for remote areas.
practical_tips: Overlanding is a great way to see the diversity of South Africa. It requires proper planning and a suitable vehicle.

description: South Africa is a year-round destination, so it’s great to visit different parts of the country throughout the year. However, the peak season for safaris is between the months of June and October. Peak Season (Nov–Feb) is summer, ideal for beaches and the Garden Route, but prices are higher. Shoulder Season (Mar–May, Sep–Oct) offers mild weather, perfect for wildlife viewing, with fewer tourists. Low Season (Jun–Aug) is winter, colder in some areas but great for whale watching in Hermanus.
practical_tips: South Africa is more affordable than Europe/US with top-tier services. It offers diversity—beaches, mountains, deserts, and wildlife in one trip.

description: Avoid certain areas in Johannesburg at night. Driving is on the left-hand side. Self-drive the Garden Route, but join guided tours in wildlife zones. Malaria risk in Kruger—take prophylaxis. Buy a local SIM card for good coverage. Cards are widely accepted, but cash is handy in small towns.
practical_tips: A common misconception is that it’s not a safe place to visit. Like in any city, be mindful of where you go depending on the time of day, but overall it’s a safe destination. You’re usually with a guide, which gives you the local experience too.

description: Little Bush Camp in the Sabi Sand Private Game Reserve is a great place to stay. Cape Town offers a range of accommodations from boutique hotels to waterfront properties. Spending a good amount of your budget on a lodge stay can really change your experience.
practical_tips: Sabi Sand
column9: Book well in advance for peak safari season (June–October).
column10: An ideal itinerary includes three nights in Cape Town, three nights in a private game reserve in Kruger National Park, and then three or four nights in Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe, with a day trip to Chobe National Park in Botswana.

description: Day 1-3: Cape Town – Table Mountain, Cape of Good Hope, penguins, wine estates. Day 4-5: Garden Route (self-drive) – Mossel Bay → Knysna → Tsitsikamma. Day 6-7: Kruger National Park – Safari to find the Big Five.
practical_tips: Kruger
column9: Best in shoulder seasons (Mar–May, Sep–Oct) for fewer crowds.
column10: This itinerary covers the best of South Africa’s diversity—city, coast, and wildlife.

description: Day 1-3: Cape Town – Table Mountain, Cape of Good Hope, wine estates. Day 4-5: Garden Route – Knysna, Tsitsikamma.
practical_tips: A shorter trip focused on the Western Cape’s highlights.

description: Day 1: Table Mountain + Signal Hill sunset. Day 2: Cape of Good Hope + penguins. Day 3: Wine estates + city tour.
practical_tips: A quick Cape Town express itinerary for travelers with limited time.

description: The Victoria & Albert Waterfront in Cape Town has so many amazing restaurants to pick from right on the water. It is a great place to eat and enjoy gorgeous coastal views.
practical_tips: The V&A Waterfront is a top dining destination. It offers a wide range of restaurants and is a great place to enjoy South African cuisine.

description: Buy a local SIM card in advance or download Google offline maps. A European-style round-pin adapter is a must. Pack stomach medicine as local food can easily cause discomfort. High-SPF sunscreen and cooling sleeves are essential in summer.
practical_tips: Egypt is beautiful—the pyramids, temples, and the Red Sea are each breathtakingly stunning. But it is also 'exhausting' due to the need to be constantly on guard against scams.

description: Book gorilla-trekking permits well in advance as they’re limited and in high demand during dry months. Pack for a shower in any month as this is rainforest. The drier windows of June to September and December to February make trekking easier and the trails less muddy.
practical_tips: Gorillas are tracked every day of the year. A one-week trip allows you to take in Kigali’s sights, gorilla trekking, volcano hikes, and chimpanzee tracking.

description: Malaria risk in Kruger—take prophylaxis. Buy a local SIM card for good coverage. Cards are widely accepted, but cash is handy in small towns. Driving is on the left-hand side.
practical_tips: South Africa is a year-round destination. It fulfills every fantasy of adventure and luxury—whether road-tripping along the Garden Route or tracking the Big Five.
